welcome.title: Intermittent fasting, made fun
welcome.body: Tap start when you stop eating. FastFast keeps time and tells you when you hit your goal.

habit.title: Streak & Habit strength
habit.body: Every completed fast keeps your streak and fills your habit bar. Longer fasts fill it faster.

shield.title: Shields — rest days that keep your streak
shield.body: Stay consistent or finish a long fast to earn shields. On a rest day, a shield protects your streak automatically.

pixel.title: A colorful year
pixel.body: Every day is a pixel. Log your mood and weight, and see your whole year in one picture.

health.title: Listen to your body
health.body: FastFast is not a substitute for medical advice. If you are pregnant, have a medical condition or plan to fast longer than 48 hours, talk to a doctor. Stop right away if you feel dizzy or unusually unwell.

shield.title: Shield
shield.message: Shields keep your streak valid on rest days when you don't fast.
shield.effect1: Each empty day between two fasts uses 1 shield. Your streak stays valid and your Habit is unchanged.
shield.effect2: Rest without shields left and your streak breaks, Habit drops and Retain resets to 0.
shield.effect3: You can hold up to {{max}} shields; extra ones are lost.
shield.long1: Fast 48h+ to earn 1 shield, 72h+ to earn 2.
shield.long2: Rest is part of a long fast: your body needs time to refeed and recover. Shields let you rest on those days while your streak stays valid.
shield.milestone1: Reaching 35%, 70% and 100% Habit gives 1 shield each.
shield.milestone2: If your Habit drops and climbs back, you can earn the milestone again.
shield.retain1: Once Habit is at 100%, points from each fast go into Retain.

body.title: What do these bars mean?
body.message: Each bar shows how much fasting supports one of your body's built-in processes.
body.always1: These processes always run in your body, even when you're not fasting.
body.always2: They aren't switches that only turn on at a certain hour.
body.levels1: Each level means fasting supports that process more, rising with fasting time.
body.levels2: A full bar doesn't mean the process is at its strongest right now, only that fasting's support is higher.
body.estimate1: The hour marks are guesses and vary by person: your last meal, activity, sleep…
body.estimate2: This is not a diagnosis or medical advice.

tip.disableHint: You can turn off tips in Settings → Beginner tips

habit.title: How is Habit calculated?
habit.line1: Each fast of 16h or more: +3%, plus 0.2% per hour beyond 16h (20h → +3.8%).
habit.line3: Each empty day between fasts uses 1 shield. With no shields left, Habit drops — the longer the break, the bigger the drop.
habit.line4: At 100%: points move to Retain, and 25 Retain becomes 1 shield.

16h.label: Intermittent
16h.title: Popular & easy to start
16h.description: Helps your body use stored fat for energy and improves insulin sensitivity.
16h.adviceLong: This is the gold standard and the easiest to keep up. Just skip breakfast and fit all your calories into a 12pm–8pm eating window. Drink about 2L of water while fasting.

18h.label: Fat Burner
18h.title: Boosted fat burning
18h.description: Extends ketosis and starts touching on autophagy.
18h.adviceLong: Two extra hours beyond 16/8 help maximize fat burning and start autophagy. During these 18 hours you can have black coffee or unsweetened green tea to get past hunger.

20h.label: Warrior
20h.title: Warrior mode
20h.description: Maximizes fat burning and helps preserve muscle mass.
20h.advice: (20h) A 4-hour eating window. Get enough protein.
20h.adviceLong: The eating window is very short (only 4 hours). Focus on enough protein (meat, fish, eggs) and fiber to keep your muscles. Avoid eating too fast, which can overload digestion.

23h.label: OMAD
23h.title: One meal a day
23h.description: Promotes autophagy and gives your digestive system a deep rest.
23h.advice: (23h) Your one meal should be fully nutritious.
23h.adviceLong: A nearly full 24-hour fast (e.g. dinner today, then nothing until dinner tomorrow). That single meal should be whole foods, rich in healthy fats and protein. Listen to your body if you do this often.

36h.label: Monk
36h.title: Through-the-day challenge
36h.description: Gives your gut a long recovery window and helps calm inflammation.
36h.advice: (36h) Pick a day with little heavy activity.
36h.adviceLong: A full day and night without food (e.g. finish dinner on Monday, skip Tuesday, eat again Wednesday morning). Choose a light workday and add electrolytes (mineral salts) to stay alert.

48h.label: Extended
48h.title: Advanced deep fast
48h.description: Fully depletes stored glycogen, pushing your body to restructure how it uses energy.
48h.adviceLong: A fast this long requires daily electrolytes (salt, potassium, magnesium) to keep your blood pressure stable. If you feel faint or dizzy for a long time, break your fast right away.

72h.label: Prolonged
72h.title: Ultimate challenge
72h.description: Reaches deep autophagy. Needs careful preparation and caution.
72h.adviceLong: Only do this occasionally, once your body is very used to fasting. When breaking the fast, never start with a big meal; begin with bone broth or something light to protect your stomach.

info.title: Reading your Journey
info.message: What the icon legend doesn't cover.
info.fast1: Each cell is colored by the total length of the longest fast that touches that day.
info.fast2: A fast spanning several days colors all of them, lighter on the first day and darker toward the end.
info.fast3: A cell with a shield icon is a rest day protected by a shield.
info.mood1: A cell with a primary-colored border is a day with a note.
info.action1: Tap an empty day to add a mood and note; tap a day with data to see details.
info.action2: The number under each icon is how many days of the year fall into that level.
info.action3: Use the Week/Day button in the grid corner to change the layout. Saved images follow the current layout.
